hints: A modulus graph reflects the part of the line y=3x−2a below the x-axis.
Solve 3x−2a=0 for the vertex and evaluate the function at x=0 for the y-intercept.
Draw two straight rays meeting at the vertex, with branches extending into both the first and second quadrants.
walkthrough:
Find the vertex of the modulus function $y = |3x - 2a|$ by setting the expression inside to zero:
$$3x - 2a = 0 \implies 3x = 2a \implies x = \dfrac{2a}{3}$$
$$\text{The vertex lies on the positive } x\text{-axis at } \left(\dfrac{2a}{3}, 0\right).$$

Find the $y$-intercept by substituting $x = 0$:
$$y = |3(0) - 2a| = |-2a| = 2a \quad (\text{since } a > 0)$$
$$\text{The } y\text{-intercept is at } (0, 2a).$$

Define the two linear branches:
$$\text{Right branch } \left(x \geqslant \dfrac{2a}{3}\right): \quad y = 3x - 2a \quad (\text{slope } +3)$$
$$\text{Left branch } \left(x < \dfrac{2a}{3}\right): \quad y = -(3x - 2a) = 2a - 3x \quad (\text{slope } -3)$$
$$\text{Sketch the symmetrical V-shaped graph with straight rays extending into the first and second quadrants.}$$

ai_rubric.Sketching Modulus Graphs: Concludes that symmetrical V-shaped graph with vertex $(\frac{2a}{3},0)$, straight branches in the first and second quadrants, and $y$-intercept $2a$.

hints: For |3x−2a|<x+5a, compare the line x+5a with each branch of the modulus graph.
Solve x+5a=3x−2a and x+5a=2a−3x to locate the two boundary values, using a>0 to order them.
The strict inequality holds where the line lies above the V; state the open interval between the crossings.
walkthrough:
Solve the boundary equation for the positive branch $3x - 2a = x + 5a$:
$$3x - x = 5a + 2a$$
$$2x = 7a \implies x = \dfrac{7a}{2}$$

Solve the boundary equation for the negative branch $-(3x - 2a) = x + 5a$:
$$2a - 3x = x + 5a$$
$$-3x - x = 5a - 2a$$
$$-4x = 3a \implies x = -\dfrac{3a}{4}$$

Verify that the boundary line $y = x + 5a$ is positive at both critical values:
$$\text{At } x = -\dfrac{3a}{4}: \quad -\dfrac{3a}{4} + 5a = \dfrac{17a}{4} > 0$$
$$\text{At } x = \dfrac{7a}{2}: \quad \dfrac{7a}{2} + 5a = \dfrac{17a}{2} > 0$$

State the solution interval where the V-shaped graph lies strictly below the line $y = x + 5a$:
$$-\dfrac{3a}{4} < x < \dfrac{7a}{2}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Inequalities: Derives critical value $\frac{7a}{2}$ from $x+5a=3x-2a$. Identifies Concludes with $-\frac{3a}{4}<x<\frac{7a}{2}$. The final result is $-\dfrac{3a}{4}<x<\dfrac{7a}{2}$.
